topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines the key learning outcomes, and establishes the clinical and biological scope of cancer biology.

topics.label: Biological origins of cancer and tissue disruption
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how the accumulation of genetic and epigenetic alterations causes cancer by disrupting normal cellular differentiation, tissue architecture, and cell-matrix interactions.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and benign-to-malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the pathological differences between benign and malignant tumors, focusing on basement membrane invasion, metastatic routes, and the stepwise progression from pre-invasive polyps to invasive carcinomas.

topics.label: Tumor classification and nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and exceptions used to name benign and malignant tumors based on their tissue and cellular lineage of origin.

topics.label: Pathophysiological mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physical, functional, and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors impair normal physiology to cause illness and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across human organs and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the epidemiological distribution of common cancer types in humans and compare cancer patterns across companion animals and diverse multicellular taxa.

topics.label: Principles and modalities of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical rationale, diagnostic techniques, and relative efficacy of screening programs aimed at detecting pre-malignant lesions and early-stage tumors.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and upcoming practicals
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture with a review of the learning objectives and instructions for upcoming practical sessions.
